License CC-BY-3.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Selected original facts are transcribed with original project scope notes; no source assets are bundled or relicensed under project MIT.

J. Micromech. Microeng. 24 (2014) 035017. Original Table 2 100 °C tensile-cure result; 95% confidence interval with unspecified estimand/construction, six test samples averaged, source-applied 0.40 strain correction retained without reapplication.

2026-11-03 supplement: five existing Table 1 tensile-cure states retain their Young moduli and gain Table 2 explicitly labelled ultimate tensile strengths. Source-stated 95% CI and six tensile samples retained with unknown estimand/construction/peak-averaging order. Section 3.1 versus 4.1 strength-window wording remains unresolved and is explicitly recorded; no stress recalculation or source repair. Earlier 100 °C note describes the initial selected result, not current coverage. CC BY3.0 attribution and source-asset exclusion remain.

method_definition.definition: Source-labelled Table 2 ultimate tensile strength from Hounsfield Universal 10 kN tensile testing, ASTM D412 Type C, crosshead 254 mm/min. Source section 3.1 includes maximum strength in a below-40%-strain computation statement, whereas section 4.1 describes a nonlinear region before failure. Strength extraction range and peak/averaging algorithm remain unresolved; no source value is recalculated.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.3–4 section 3.1; p.4 section 4.1 and Figure 3; p.5 Table 2

source_discrepancies.description: Section 3.1 groups Young modulus, maximum tensile strength and elongation at break in a below-40%-strain computation statement; section 4.1 describes a nonlinear region before failure and Figure 3 extends beyond 40%. Strength extraction range/algorithm cannot be resolved. Keep Table 2 explicitly labelled UTS values with an explicit discrepancy; do not silently assign the Young modulus window to UTS.
source_discrepancies.disposition: Retain source-labelled Table 2 UTS and its CI as a catalog-only reported result. Do not repair source wording, assert a verified below-40% or full-curve extraction algorithm, reapply strain correction to stress, or use the result as an engineering allowable.
